title: How much does an AI demo agent cost per month in 2026?
summary: AI demo agent pricing in 2026: public prices for 9 tools, the 4 pricing models, hidden costs and a simple ROI check. Under $500 or over $2,000 a month?
body_markdown:
An AI demo agent that shows your real product to leads on a call usually costs $750 to $2,500 a month at entry, and more than $2,000 a month once a sales team runs it at real volume. Under $500 a month buys a credit-metered agent on top of an interactive tour tool, or a low-volume starter plan; Karumi, like most live-product agents, prices by quote after a short scoping call.


Karumi is an AI demo agent: an autonomous agent that shows a buyer your real product live, by voice or chat, and answers questions as it goes. Below: what nine AI demo agents and interactive demo tools charge on their own pricing pages as of November 2026, and how to work out what you would pay.


## Is an AI demo agent under $500 or over $2,000 a month?


Both exist. The price follows what the agent does.


What you buy Typical monthly price (November 2026) What the lead gets


Interactive tour plus a metered chat agent $0 to $500 A clickable tour with an agent that answers questions


Low-volume AI demo plan $250 to $750 A set number of AI demos a month, often slides or captures


Live-product demo agent for one team $750 to $2,500 An agent that runs your real product, by voice or chat


Agent at sales-team volume, many languages, CRM sync Over $2,000, usually annual Many agents, use cases and markets, with security reviews


If the agent must show your real product to leads on a live call, plan for the upper rows. If you only need answers on top of a recorded tour, the lower rows are enough.


## How are AI demo agents priced?


Vendors use four models, often two in one contract.


- **Flat plan.** One price a month or a year, sized by agents, volume, languages and integrations. Karumi, Walnut and Consensus sell this way. It is easy to budget, but read what the plan caps.
- **Per seat or per creator.** You pay for each person who builds demos. Storylane, Supademo and LiveDemo use it for their tour products. The agent is often a separate line.
- **Per session or per demo.** You pay for engaged demos or conversations. Naoma bills per engaged demo, and Navattic prices its agents by conversations and agents. Cost follows usage, so a good month costs more.
- **Per minute or per credit.** You buy credits or minutes of agent time. Supademo charges one credit per agent response plus one credit per 15 seconds of voice. LiveDemo includes 60 minutes of avatar credits a month on Growth.

What each one does well:


- **Naoma** is the most transparent. It publishes every tier, and demos pause at the limit, so there are no surprise charges. Floe's tracker notes that the Starter plan covers slide-based demos and that live product walkthroughs start on Growth.
- **Storylane** and **Supademo** are cheap to start, with free plans and low per-seat prices for tours.
- **Walnut** includes CRM sync and its agent on the entry plan, which removes one tier jump.
- **Navattic** has a free plan and a startup program.
- **LiveDemo** is the cheapest way to try an AI avatar, and its code can be self-hosted for free.
- **Consensus** , **Floe** and **Karumi** quote by volume, which fits teams that want a pilot before a contract.


Karumi does not publish a list price. Its[pricing page](https://karumi.ai/pricing) says pricing depends on the number of agents, expected demo volume, languages and integrations, and that most teams start with a pilot on one use case. Some third-party lists still quote an older Karumi figure; ask for a quote at your volume.


## What moves the price of an AI demo agent?


Five things move the price more than the vendor.


1. **Live product or capture.** An agent that drives your real product must sign in, handle changes and stay accurate. A tour or a slide deck is cheaper to run. Read[is a Karumi demo live or a recording](https://karumi.ai/blog/is-karumi-demo-live-or-recording) for the difference.
2. **Voice or chat.** Voice costs more to run. Supademo, for example, adds a credit for every 15 seconds of agent audio.
3. **Volume.** Demos, conversations or visitors a month. This is the main driver in per-session and per-credit models.
4. **Languages and markets.** Each language is more content to keep correct. Karumi lists languages as a pricing factor.
5. **Integrations and security.** CRM sync, SSO and security reviews often sit on higher tiers. On Karumi, CRM export is in Growth, and SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, on-premise deployment and SLAs are in Enterprise.


## What hidden costs should you check?


The plan price is rarely the full bill. Check these before you sign.


- **The agent is a separate line.** On many tour tools, the AI agent is an add-on billed by credits, visitors or conversations. It can cost more than the base plan.
- **Annual-only billing.** Walnut and Navattic's paid plans are billed annually. A monthly-looking price is a yearly commitment.
- **Credit limits.** Ask what happens at the limit. Naoma pauses demos. Walnut pauses AI. Others sell top-up packs.
- **Tier jumps.** One gated feature, such as Salesforce sync or SSO, can push you up a tier. On Storylane, Salesforce starts on Premium at $1,200 a month yearly.
- **Setup, upkeep and review.** Someone connects the agent to your product, prepares a demo account with safe data, keeps it current when the product changes and reads early transcripts. Ask who does this work, you or the vendor.


## How do you estimate the ROI of an AI demo agent?


Compare the agent's monthly cost with what the same demos cost you today:


1. **Demos a month.** How many first demos your team runs, plus the requests that never get one.
2. **Cost per human demo.** Rep and sales engineer hours per demo, times their loaded hourly cost.
3. **Lost demand.** Leads that go cold while they wait. Our post on[the cost of demo wait](https://karumi.ai/blog/cost-of-demo-wait) shows how to size it.


A worked example with assumed inputs: your team runs 120 first demos a month. Each takes 1.5 hours of rep and sales engineer time at $80 an hour, so each human demo costs $120, or $14,400 a month. An agent at $2,000 a month that handles half of those first demos saves $7,200 a month in time. Lost demand comes on top. For the full method, use our guide on[how to calculate the ROI of demo automation tools](https://karumi.ai/blog/how-to-calculate-roi-demo-automation-tools) .


Two numbers matter more than the plan price:


- **Cost per completed demo.** Plan price divided by the demos you expect. Naoma's Growth plan, for example, works out to $7.50 per demo at full use.
- **Cost per qualified meeting.** Plan price divided by meetings booked. Compare it with your SDR cost.


## What do you get from Karumi for the price?


Karumi prices by agents, volume, languages and integrations because that is what the agent does. It is not a recording, a replica or a scripted tour.


- **The real product, live.** The agent decides what to show in your actual product and adapts to each buyer. See[how Karumi works](https://karumi.ai/blog/how-does-karumi-work) .
- **Voice and chat.** Buyers talk or type. Call agents also run voice campaigns.
- **Live calls.** The agent[joins Google Meet, Zoom and Teams calls](https://karumi.ai/blog/can-karumi-join-google-meet-zoom-teams-calls) , so a lead can get a demo on a call without waiting for a rep.
- **The buyer's language.** A demo link sets the language for each lead.
- **Outbound and booking.** A live demo link goes into a cold email, and the agent ends on the right rep's calendar.
- **CRM and analytics.** Sessions sync to HubSpot, Salesforce and Attio with transcripts, summaries and qualification data, and every session is recorded with analytics.


In our experience, buyers ask about pricing early, often before they have seen the product. An agent that answers price and fit questions on the spot, then books the call, earns its cost faster than a tour. If you are still deciding whether to build or buy, read[build vs buy an AI demo agent](https://karumi.ai/blog/build-vs-buy-ai-demo-agent) .


## FAQ


### How much does an AI demo agent cost per month?


Published prices run from free tiers to $2,083 a month or more, as of November 2026. An agent that shows your real product on a live call usually costs $750 to $2,500 a month at entry, and more at sales-team volume. Many vendors, Karumi included, quote by volume.


### Is there a free AI demo agent?


Some tour tools include free agent usage. Supademo gives every workspace 1,500 free agent credits, and LiveDemo is free for one creator.


### Why do so many AI demo agents not publish prices?


The cost depends on volume, languages, voice use and integrations. A live-product agent also needs setup on your product. Vendors such as Karumi, Floe and Consensus scope a quote, and most offer a pilot first.


### Does Karumi publish its price?


No. Karumi's pricing page lists Growth and Enterprise plans, and says pricing depends on agents, demo volume, languages and integrations. Most teams start with a pilot on one use case.


### What is cheaper, per seat or per demo pricing?


Per seat is cheaper when few people build demos and volume is high. Per demo is cheaper when volume is low or seasonal. Compare on cost per completed demo.


### What should I ask a vendor before I buy?


Ask what a session, credit or demo is, and what happens at the limit. Ask which features sit on a higher tier, whether billing is annual, and who sets up and maintains the agent when your product changes.
